ThemeImageDetails: Digital, large-digital, square analog and flip clock styles, with adjustable position, type size, order and weather.

ThemeCryptoDetails: Two to four coins from Binance with the live price, 24-hour change and a 24-hour sparkline for each.
ThemePomodoroDetails: A focus/break timer on the keyboard screen: a countdown ring, the current phase and completed cycles. Start and stop it from settings or the tray menu.
ThemeHardwareDescription: Temps, clocks, fans and VRAM on rotating pages

ThemeGitHubDescription: The contribution graph as a dot matrix

ThemeCalendarDetails: Today's and the upcoming events from a calendar's ICS link (Google, Apple and Outlook all offer one), refreshed every five minutes. Simple repeating events are understood; exotic recurrence rules are shown by their first occurrence only.
ThemeCountdownDetails: Up to three dates to look forward to: the nearest one large with the days, hours or minutes left, the others in rows below. Dates are set in the theme's settings and live only on this machine.
ThemeWorldClockDescription: Up to four cities side by side
ThemeWorldClockDetails: The local time in up to four places, each with its offset from your clock and a night tint between 22:00 and 07:00. Time zones are entered as IANA names such as Europe/Kyiv or America/New_York.
ThemePingDetails: ICMP latency to up to four hosts - the router, a DNS resolver, your server - with a bar history where lost pings stay visible as gaps. Green under 60 ms, orange under 150 ms, red beyond or unreachable.
ThemeDisksDetails: Every ready volume with its used space as a bar - the accent color until 85%, orange to 95%, red beyond. Up to six volumes fit on the screen.
ThemeComposerDescription: Build your own layout from widgets
ThemeComposerDetails: A stack of small widgets you pick and order yourself: clocks, system counters, weather, rates, alerts and more.

RiskClaudeHeading: Counted here, not reported by Anthropic
RiskClaudeBody:
This screen adds up the tokens in Claude Code's own transcripts on this computer. Nothing is sent anywhere, and no login or key is asked for.

Two things follow from that. It only sees Claude Code on this machine, so the total is a floor on your account's real usage, not the account total. And Anthropic publishes no quota that software can read, so the meters fill against a budget you set yourself - a percentage of your own target, not an official limit.

CurrencyQuotesHint: Comma-separated ISO codes, e.g. EUR, UAH, PLN. Up to four fit on the screen.

Units12HourHint: The small screen shows no AM/PM marker - only the digits change.

AlertsHint: Data comes from the community alerts.in.ua API and refreshes every half minute. This screen is informational, with inherent delays - never your only warning source.

ThemeAccentHint: This theme can keep its own accent color; without one it follows the global accent from the Screen page.
WorldClockHint: Up to four places. The label is free text; the time zone is an IANA name such as Europe/Kyiv, America/New_York or Asia/Tokyo.

HardwareSensorsUnsupported: Running as administrator, and this board still reports no temperature
PerfVisualValuesHint: Shows the current figure on each panel next to its curve.
HardwareLimitedSensors: Limited sensors - run as administrator for temperatures and fans
KnobHint: Switch themes with the Linx68 volume knob: turn right for the next theme, left for the previous, press to pause or resume the carousel. Off by default.
KnobSuppressHint: On: the knob only switches themes and the system volume stays put. Off: it does both at once.
KnobVidPidHint: Optional and blunt: a knob and the same keyboard's Fn volume keys share one VID:PID, so this binds the whole keyboard. Prefer detection below; empty reacts to any volume key.
KnobViaHint: Cleanest with VIA/QMK: remap the encoder to F13/F14 and its press to F15 in the keyboard's configurator, pick the dedicated-keys mode here, and volume is never touched at all.
CurrencySourceHint: If a rate looks off, switch the source - the screen's footer shows which day the data is for. The NBU option uses Ukraine's official daily rate, crossing other pairs through UAH.
RiskAlertsBody: This screen reads active alerts from the community alerts.in.ua API with a token you request yourself. The data passes through third-party infrastructure and arrives with delays of seconds to minutes; the app polls it every half minute. Treat it as a convenience display only - always rely on official sirens and government alert channels, never on this screen, for your safety decisions. The token is stored on this machine and sent only to alerts.in.ua.
RiskTelegramHeading: The session key stays on this machine
RiskTelegramBody: You sign in to your own Telegram account through the official MTProto API (via the open-source WTelegramClient library). The login creates a session key - the most sensitive piece of data this app stores. It is kept in a file on this machine, is sent only to Telegram's servers, and 'Log out' wipes it. api_id, api_hash and your phone number are stored in the settings file as plain text. Message popups are drawn on the keyboard screen only; nothing is forwarded anywhere. If anyone else uses this computer, prefer the count-only privacy mode and log out when done.
RiskGitHubBody: Without a token, KSS fetches the public contribution page for the username you enter, over HTTPS, from github.com. If you add a token, it is kept in this machine's settings file as plain text and sent only to api.github.com - use a fine-grained token with no extra permissions, treat it like a password, and revoke it at any time in your GitHub settings.
KnobBoundNone: Not detected yet - every volume key counts as the knob
KnobDetectHint: Detection learns the HID collection the knob itself speaks on, which is what separates it from the same keyboard's Fn volume keys - a VID:PID cannot, because they share one. It takes precedence over the field above.
KnobDetectResultBound: Done - the knob is bound to {0}. The other volume keys are left alone.
KnobDetectResultHotKeys: The knob already sends plain keys ({0}), so volume is never involved. Switch the input mode to dedicated keys and pick them there.
KnobDetectResultNothing: No volume report arrived. Check that the knob is turning and that the keyboard is connected.
KnobDetectResultSame: This keyboard sends the knob and the volume keys through one HID collection with the same usages, so nothing can tell them apart. Remap the encoder to F13-F24 in VIA/QMK and switch to dedicated-keys mode.
KnobDetectStep1Hint: Turn it several times in both directions and press it. Volume still works while detecting - nothing is swallowed yet.
KnobDetectStep2: Step 2 of 2: press the other volume keys
KnobDetectStep2Hint: Use the keyboard's Fn volume keys - the ones that must keep controlling the volume. Skip if this keyboard has none.
ClaudeCheckLineOk: OK - {0} tokens this week, read from {1}
ComposerHint: Stack widgets top to bottom - the preview shows the result live.
ComposerBudgetOverflow: Widgets past the limit are hidden
ClaudeLocalSourceHint: Read from Claude Code's own transcripts on this PC. No login, no key, nothing to install - and nothing that can be blocked. Counts cover this machine only, so they are a floor on your real usage.
ClaudeBudgetHint: Anthropic publishes no readable quota, so the meters fill against a target you set. Pick the plan for a starting point, then adjust once you have seen a week of your own use.
